ai.title: Add ephemeral cache control to AI SDK message transform
ai.summary: Updated `transformMessages` in `backend/src/llm-apis/vercel-ai-sdk/ai-sdk.ts` to propagate `cache_control` flags as `providerOptions.cacheControl` with type `ephemeral`. This ensures user, assistant, and tool messages respect upstream cache directives when sent via the Vercel AI SDK. Scope limited to the backend LLM API adapter.

eli5.text: When the system builds messages to send to an AI model, it now carries over special caching instructions attached to user, assistant, and tool messages. If a message contains a cache-control marker, it is passed along as an ephemeral cache directive, telling the AI service it is okay to temporarily store that part of the conversation for faster follow-up requests. The change affects every conversation that uses this internal message-preparation path, which runs behind the scenes whenever messages are forwarded through the AI integration layer. You will not see this directly, but repeated identical or near-identical prompts that were previously reprocessed each time can now be served from a short-term cache.

eli5.text: When you ask an assistant to generate text, it can now stop generating as soon as it hits any of the phrases you specified as stop words. Previously, even if you gave it stop words, it would ignore them and keep going. This only affects the internal tool that connects to one specific AI model, so if you never used stop words before, you won't notice anything different. You don't need to do anything to turn it on. It's live now.

ai.title: Fix mock leakage in usage-calculation tests
ai.summary: Refactored test structure in backend/src/__tests__/usage-calculation.test.ts and auto-topup.test.ts to prevent mock leakage. Moved mock.reset() and mock.module() calls from individual it() blocks to a top-level beforeEach() hook. This ensures clean state isolation between tests and fixes flaky failures caused by stale mocks.

eli5.text: Tests that calculate credit usage and auto-recharge behavior were occasionally failing at random because leftover fake data from one test was 'leaking' into the next. The code now clears all fake data in one shared setup step before every test runs, so each test starts with a clean slate. You would see fewer surprise failures on the testing dashboard, especially in the billing and usage tests that had been flaky.

ai.title: Fix unsafe non-null assertion in uploadExpandedFileContextForTraining
ai.summary: Replaced unsafe non-null assertions (`!`) with explicit null/undefined checks in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`. This prevents potential runtime crashes when accessing `loadedFiles` entries that may not exist. The change affects the `uploadExpandedFileContextForTraining` function, ensuring safer iteration over file contents before token counting.

eli5.text: When the assistant needs to gather background from documents before answering, it now skips any file it can't actually find instead of crashing. Previously, if a referenced file wasn't loaded in memory, the process would hit an unexpected stop and fail; now it quietly moves on to the next usable file. This makes gathering file context a bit more reliable for anyone using the assistant's file-aware workflows. The fix is live today.

ai.title: Fix Anthropic prompt caching provider options and track cache tokens
ai.summary: Moved `cacheControl` into `providerOptions.anthropic` for user, assistant, and tool messages in `transformMessages` to match Vercel AI SDK expectations. Extracted `cacheReadInputTokens` and `cacheCreationInputTokens` from `providerMetadata.anthropic` in `promptAiSdkStream` and persisted them via `saveMessage`. Updated `backend/src/llm-apis/vercel-ai-sdk/ai-sdk.ts`.

eli5.text: Prompts that the assistant and tools send to Anthropic’s Claude can now be cached for reuse, which should lower costs and speed up repeated requests. When a cacheable message is received, the system now places the caching instruction in the correct spot that Anthropic expects, and it also records how many tokens were saved or used to create the cache, storing that information alongside each interaction. This only affects internal routing and billing details, so most users will just see faster or cheaper responses without any visible change to the interface.

ai.title: Squash system messages in Vercel AI SDK transform
ai.summary: Squashes multiple system message blocks into a single string in `transformMessages` within `backend/src/llm-apis/vercel-ai-sdk/ai-sdk.ts`. Previously, array-based system inputs were pushed as individual `CoreMessage` objects. Now, they are joined with `\n\n` into a single `system` role message.

eli5.text: When you send instructions to the assistant, any set of separate instruction blocks now gets combined into one clear, single message instead of being sent as a stack of individual snippets. This affects how your instructions are passed to the assistant's backend, and you'd notice it only if you were inspecting the internal flow. The change is live today and is a behind-the-scenes tweak to keep the message format consistent.

ai.summary: Reordered `sendCostResponseToClient` to execute before database storage operations in `saveMessage` within `backend/src/llm-apis/message-cost-tracker.ts`. Eliminates client-side latency caused by waiting for the database write to complete before receiving the cost calculation. Internal logic update affecting the message saving pipeline.

eli5.text: When you send a message that costs credits, you now get the cost reply immediately instead of waiting for the system to finish saving your message first. The platform simply tells you how many credits you were charged before it writes that information to its internal records, so you never sit watching a loading screen while the database catches up. This only affects people sending messages through the assistant chat today.

ai.title: Persist partial eval results during git eval runs
ai.summary: Git eval runner now writes partial results to a trace-ID-suffixed file after each commit. Prevents data loss on crash or timeout by incrementally persisting state. Scope limited to evals/git-evals/run-git-evals.ts. Final output still written to a distinct trace-ID-suffixed file upon completion.

eli5.text: When the system runs a batch of evaluations (tests of how well an AI assistant works on different code changes), it now saves its progress to a file after checking each individual result. If something goes wrong or times out halfway through, the work done so far is no longer lost and can be recovered. You would see partial results saved in a file with a unique tag in its name after each step, and a final complete results file written separately when everything finishes.

ai.title: Improve error handling and timeouts in git evals runner
ai.summary: Added process-level uncaughtException and unhandledRejection handlers to capture async errors during single eval runs. Wrapped agent decision prompts with 5-minute timeouts and loopMainPrompt execution with 30-minute timeouts using withTimeout utility. Improved error logging and ensured judging results are returned even if judging fails.

eli5.text: The automated eval system is now more careful about catching failures that happen while running code-generation tests. When an eval session crashes unexpectedly or a sub-task hangs, the system still logs what went wrong and delivers the partial judging results instead of dropping them entirely. This makes the internal test harness more reliable for the team that runs git-based evals, but it does not change anything you see as an end user today.

ai.title: Fix Saxy entity detection for ampersands
ai.summary: Saxy now checks the full post-ampersand string slice instead of only the next single character to determine if a potential entity is pending. This prevents premature flushing of incomplete entities like `&#` or short named entities when chunk boundaries fall immediately after `&`. The fix applies to the `common/src/util/saxy.ts` XML/HTML parser stream. Duplicate trailing entity checks were removed to consolidate logic.

eli5.text: If you paste or send text that contains an ampersand (`&`) followed by a partial entity, such as a lone `&#` or a short named entity, the system will no longer cut it off at the boundary between chunks; it now holds the remainder and waits for the rest of the entity to arrive before treating it as text. This only affects the background component that reads XML and HTML streams, so documents with such fragments will now parse correctly instead of dropping or misreading part of the entity. The improvement is live today for anyone using that parsing step.

ai.title: Judge evals context truncation
ai.summary: Judge Git evals now smartly truncate context to fit within 1 million token limit. Mechanism iteratively removes pre/post-commit content, then truncates trace entries from end if needed. Scope: `evals/git-evals/judge-git-eval.ts`. Detail: `countTokens` from `backend/src/util/token-counter` validates prompt size against `MAX_TOKENS`.

eli5.text: When the system grades a coding assistant's work by having another AI review the full session, that review could previously get cut off if the session was too long. Now the system automatically shortens the session material it sends for review, first by dropping the full before-and-after file contents, then by trimming older trace entries, until it fits within the million-token limit. You wouldn't see a different score, but reviews that used to fail partway through will now complete.

ai.summary: New `.github/workflows/daily-git-evals.yml` runs Codebuff git evaluations daily at 8am UTC. Uses Bun 1.2.12, uploads `eval-trace-*.json` artifacts with 30-day retention, and generates step summaries. Internal CI only; no user-facing changes.

These checks save detailed reports for the team to review, and the results live in a private internal system that only staff can see. Nothing you use changes, but behind the scenes the team gets a fresh daily snapshot of AI quality.

ai.title: Git evals run 3 concurrent via async mapLimit
ai.summary: run-git-evals.ts switches sequential commit processing to concurrent execution using async.mapLimit with a cap of 3. Replaces custom mapAsync in common/src/util/promise.ts with the async library dependency. Partial results now save after each completion rather than strict iteration order. Covers evals package, adding async ^3.2.6 and @types/async ^3.2.24.

eli5.text: The system can now check three pieces of code at the same time instead of waiting for each one to finish before starting the next, which makes checking multiple code versions faster. This only affects the internal team that tests how the coding assistant behaves on different code histories, not on anyone using the assistant day to day. If you watched this testing process, you'd see it log that it's running three checks at once instead of one, and save progress files appear sooner as each batch finishes.
